skill.name: reasoning-causal
skill.description: Guides evidence-based business decisions through a six-stage causal reasoning workflow for observations, hypotheses, implications, decisions, actions, and learning.
skill.summary: Run structured causal reasoning for business decisions and operational execution.
skill.author: BellaBe

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, and ordinary business workflow terms. No command execution, network reconnaissance, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection attempt was found in the cited static contexts. A separate medium-severity governance issue remains because the workflow permits autonomous high-impact decisions under some conditions.

remediation.issue: Autonomous approval path for high-impact decisions
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before any decision that affects budgets, customers, contracts, strategy, or external commitments, even when ROI appears high.

remediation.issue: Markdown examples trigger static command-execution detectors
remediation.suggestion: Clarify that backticked paths and fenced blocks are documentation examples only and must not be executed as shell commands.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous High-Impact Business Decisions
semantic_findings.description: The skill allows AI autonomy for decisions that exceed the high-impact threshold when ROI and evidence conditions are met. This creates a governance risk if an agent has authority to commit budget, customer terms, or strategic changes without explicit user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited workflow explicitly permits autonomous high-impact decisions, but the actual impact depends on host agent permissions and user review settings.

content.value_statement: Business decisions often lose evidence, assumptions, and follow-up actions. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured causal workflow for traceable execution.
actual_capabilities: Structures decisions through input, hypothesis, implication, decision, action, and learning stages.
Connects observations to business assumptions and validation criteria.
Quantifies impact, timelines, resources, risks, and alternatives.
Creates action plans for operations, sales, marketing, and engineering threads.
Records learning outcomes and proposes updates to canvas and goal documents.
Flags high-impact decisions for human review based on impact thresholds.
limitations: Requires reliable input evidence and current business context from the user.
Does not independently verify external market data or customer claims.
May produce operational recommendations that need human approval before execution.
Best suited to known processes, not open-ended creative exploration.

use_cases.title: Assess a Product Change
use_cases.description: Evaluate a product opportunity by linking evidence to assumptions, impact, alternatives, and required actions.

use_cases.title: Manage a Sales Thread
use_cases.description: Turn a customer signal into hypotheses, deal implications, decision criteria, and follow-up tasks.

use_cases.title: Close the Learning Loop
use_cases.description: Compare expected and actual outcomes, then update assumptions, metrics, and goal status.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Causal Thread
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the causal reasoning workflow for this observation: [describe what happened]. Capture facts, context, and evidence before making any interpretation.

prompt_templates.title: Test a Business Assumption
prompt_templates.prompt: Link this observation to our current assumptions: [observation]. Create a falsifiable hypothesis, success criteria, and failure criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Decision Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this hypothesis for revenue impact, cost, timeline, risk, alternatives, and approval needs: [hypothesis and context].

prompt_templates.title: Complete the Learning Stage
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the expected outcome with these results: [results]. Identify validated assumptions, invalidated assumptions, canvas updates, goal updates, and follow-up threads.

output_examples.input: A customer asks for a premium enterprise tier with custom branding.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate the factual request from interpretation, connect it to pricing and segment assumptions, estimate revenue impact, and define decision criteria.

output_examples.input: A marketing campaign has lower conversion than expected after one week.
output_examples.output: The skill would capture the observed metrics, form a testable cause hypothesis, compare alternatives, and plan measurement actions.

output_examples.input: A completed pilot produced stronger revenue than forecast.
output_examples.output: The skill would compare predictions with results, mark supported assumptions, update metrics, and propose follow-up sales or operations threads.

best_practices: Provide concrete evidence, dates, metrics, and source links before asking for analysis.
Use human approval for commitments that affect customers, budgets, contracts, or strategic direction.
Keep each stage separate so assumptions, decisions, actions, and learning remain traceable.
anti_patterns: Using the workflow to justify a preferred decision without testing alternatives.
Skipping the input stage and starting with recommendations.
Treating generated action plans as approved external commitments.

faq.question: What kind of reasoning does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports causal reasoning for known workflows where observations can be linked to assumptions, decisions, actions, and learning.

faq.question: Can it make business decisions without a user?
faq.answer: It can structure decision logic, but users should approve commitments that affect budgets, customers, contracts, or strategy.

faq.question: Does it verify customer or market evidence?
faq.answer: No. It organizes supplied evidence and can identify gaps, but it does not independently verify external claims.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What files does the workflow produce?
faq.answer: It describes staged Markdown outputs for input, hypothesis, implication, decision, actions, and learning.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it for speculative brainstorming, legal advice, or decisions that need verified external facts before analysis.
